subject: physics_2
question_text: What happens to the weight of a body when it is charged positively?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: positive charging removes electrons; each electron has mass 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, so the body's mass and hence its weight mg decrease slightly. Matches the book's answer (printed p.19).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Electrons are removed
lines: To charge a body positively, some electrons
are removed from it. Every electron has a
mass of 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, so the mass of the
steps.margin_note: First mark. Positive charging means electrons LEAVE the body — the mass change follows from that.
steps.why: Charging never moves protons; only electrons transfer. Positive charge means a shortage of electrons, and each missing electron takes its small mass away.
common_mistakes: Saying protons are added to make the body positive. Charging transfers electrons only.
Saying the mass does not change. Each removed electron carries away 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

recall.must_convey: That positive charging removes electrons, and each electron carries away a small mass.

steps.memory_tip: Positive = electrons gone. Whatever leaves takes its mass with it.

steps.label: Weight decreases slightly
lines: Weight = mg. The mass has decreased
slightly, so the weight of the body also
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say slightly — the electron mass is tiny, so the change is very small.
steps.why: Weight is mg with g unchanged, so the weight tracks the mass exactly. The word slightly is part of the physics: the electron mass is about 10⁻³⁰ kg.
common_mistakes: Answering that the weight increases. Electrons leave a positively charged body, they do not join it.
Dropping the word slightly. The examiner looks for it — the change is real but very small.

recall.must_convey: That the weight decreases slightly because weight = mg and the mass decreased slightly.

steps.memory_tip: Follow the chain: electrons out → mass down → weight mg down, all slightly.

insider_note: The one-word trap: negatively charged would mean electrons ADDED and weight slightly increased — read which charge the question gives before writing.
